cohort: The study participants were pregnant women less than 37 weeks' gestation admitted with preterm labor or preterm prelabor rupture of membranes at Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand.
finding: Maternal ESBL-E colonization was associated with cervical procedures, prior GBS colonization, and resulted in earlier gestational age, lower birth weights, and longer hospital stays for their infants.
mod_finding: Infants born to colonized mothers had significantly higher cesarean delivery rates (100% vs. 59.3%, P = 0.01).
birth_weight: 1870 g (IQR 1485-2440) for infants of colonized mothers; 2360 g (IQR 1900-2780) for infants of noncolonized mothers
gest_age: Less than 37 weeks' gestation; 33.3 weeks (IQR 32.9-33.7) for infants of colonized mothers; 35.3 weeks (IQR 33-36.8) for infants of noncolonized mothers
